Theme

Latin word

grātum

grātum (mihi) est

phrase: the thing appreciated is the subject, or follows in a quod-clause; the person in the dative

I appreciate it, it is welcome to me

In this lexicon

  • appreciate

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 4.1.1: grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis; Cic. Fam. 2.18.1: tibi … grāta esse vehementer gaudeō

  • grātum facere: appreciate

    classical

  • grātum facere: favour

    classical

Examples

  • quās sī satis opportūnō tempore accēpistī, grātissimum mihi fēceris, sī ad mē in Ciliciam quam prīmum vēneris.

    if you have received it in good time, I’d very much appreciate it if you came to me in Cilicia as soon as possible.Cic. Fam. 2.19.2

    In the entry for appreciate

  • cupis post longum tempus neptem tuam mēque ūnā vidēre. grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis, mūtuō mehercule

    you want to see your granddaughter, and me with her, after so long. We both appreciate that you want it, and, I promise, we feel the samePlin. Ep. 4.1.1

    In the entry for appreciate

  • Amō tē, et nōn neglēxisse habeō grātiam.

    Thank you, and I appreciate your not forgetting.Ter. Ph. 54

    In the entry for appreciate
